findings.breaking_input: org.seat-assign agents = a value with a comma list where the field pattern was written for a different grammar, e.g. "researcher,planner" is fine but the tool's own re-split (space or other separator) reads a different list; also an empty names list: when read.options is empty and raw is empty string for a non-required field, names=[""] is flagged unknown.
findings.why: The membership check hard-codes a comma separator independent of the field's pattern and of how the tool splits the value. Two grammars for one value remain: the round-1 B3 fix added duplicate refusal but did not tie the separator to the declaration, so a pattern change silently desynchronises check and use.
findings.fix: Declare the separator on the field (e.g. f.list: ",") and use it in both the pattern and the split, or assert at module load that the pattern admits only the separator used here.
findings.twin_of: Two grammars for one value -> Import one pattern from its owner.

findings.breaking_input: Between readdirSync and the later run, replace entry `pilot.json` (a regular file) with a symlink or junction to a file outside the store; or an entry whose lstat is a file but whose parent `campaigns` directory is itself a symlink/junction pointing outside the tree.
findings.why: lstat is applied to the entries but never to the directory being listed (campaigns/, .claude/agents, fixtures/legal/ventures) and no realpath containment is done, so a linked parent yields entries that all lstat as regular files from outside the root. The fix closed the per-entry link but not the listing root, the exact 'realpath'ed inside the root' half of the pattern. The check is also a separate lstat from the later read by the tool (check-then-use).
findings.fix: realpath the listed directory and require it to sit inside its expected root (store path, repo .claude/agents, fixtures) before listing; refuse by name otherwise.
findings.twin_of: A listing that followed symlinks -> Each listed file is lstat'ed regular and realpath'ed inside the root, or rejected by name.

findings.breaking_input: campaigns path exists but is a regular file, or a dangling link at `campaigns`: readdirSync throws ENOTDIR.
findings.why: ENOENT is read as 'none yet' while ENOTDIR/ELOOP are failures, but a store whose `campaigns` entry is a dangling symlink reports ENOENT from readdir and is treated as empty and healthy ('none yet -- create one first'), hiding a broken store as an empty list. Empty-because-absent and empty-because-unreadable are conflated.
findings.fix: On ENOENT, lstat the path: if it exists as a link, return a named failure; only a truly absent path is empty.
findings.twin_of: A wrong-shaped source returned an empty inventory -> empty because absent and empty because unreadable are different results.

findings.breaking_input: A source failure: leadsCampaigns/legalVentures returns failure with options [] (e.g. EBUSY reading ventures.yaml). The op card's select field then has options [] with required true.
findings.why: emptyPicker treats an unreadable source the same as an empty one and the UI says 'none yet -- create one first', telling the owner to create something when the list is merely unreadable. The server-side distinction (FIELD_UNKNOWN vs empty) is lost at the card, so an unreadable list reads as 'none'.
findings.fix: Carry the source failure code on the served field and have emptyPicker/planBlocked name 'could not be read (CODE)' instead of NONE_YET.
findings.twin_of: A wrong-shaped source returned an empty inventory -> empty because absent and empty because unreadable are different results.

findings.breaking_input: The first setDeviceMetricsOverride (1366x768) itself throws or times out after partially applying; it is outside the try/finally.
findings.why: Only the evaluate is inside try/finally. If the first override send rejects after the browser applied it, the restore never runs and later rooms are measured on the 1366 frame. The round-1 fix guards the read but not the write that changes the frame.
findings.fix: Move the first setDeviceMetricsOverride inside the try so the finally always restores.
findings.twin_of: A viewport changed for one read and restored only on success -> an emulation override made for one measurement is restored in a `finally`.

findings.breaking_input: The strip renders but every button sits inside a hidden ancestor (getClientRects length 0) in all rooms, or a mutant where every room's verb is drawn at top 767 via a spacer only above the fold; also firstVerb values of -1 for 36 rooms except 1.
findings.why: judge() only requires rooms > 0, while the floor of 20 lives only in the bats wrapper. A run where 19 rooms lose their strip passes judge(); the verdict itself does not carry the promise ('23/23 rooms with verbs').
findings.fix: Give judge() a floor derived from the contract's rooms that declare ops, with a mutant at one below the floor.
findings.twin_of: A judged number with a floor below its promise -> Judge the number against what the REQ promises (every crossing), with a mutant at each failing value.

findings.breaking_input: A select value containing non-BMP or multibyte text, e.g. 80 emoji, or a value of 79 ASCII chars followed by a surrogate pair split by slice(0,80).
findings.why: slice works on UTF-16 units, so a surrogate pair can be cut in half before the replace; the lone surrogate is then replaced by '?', fine, but the cap counts units not characters, and options.join(', ') in the same message is uncapped: a source holding hundreds of names makes the refusal line unbounded and it travels to the page and logs.
findings.fix: Cap the joined option list (e.g. first 20 names plus a count) in the refusal message.
findings.twin_of: An unbounded fragment beside a capped buffer -> cap the line as well as the buffer.

findings.breaking_input: A plan for money.close-month made at the last second of a month, applied after the window rolls; or an op whose plan-time values were accepted by a source read, then a transient source failure at apply.
findings.why: Re-validation re-reads the picker sources (and the wall clock) outside the claim, so a transient reader failure surfaces as OPTION_GONE ('no longer offered') because failures arrive as BAD_INPUT from an empty options list, not as FIELD_UNKNOWN. The comment promises the distinction, but validateInput throws BAD_INPUT for an unreadable select source (read.options empty) whenever the read carries a failure only if it throws a different code, which the diff does not show.
findings.fix: Have validateInput throw FIELD_UNKNOWN when read.failure is non-empty before the membership test, and pin it with a test that makes the source fail between plan and apply.
findings.twin_of: One refusal code for "the list moved" and "the list is unreadable" -> a value that left its list after the plan is OPTION_GONE; a source that cannot be read stays FIELD_UNKNOWN.
